title: Typed array not checking a variable's type when its value is <Freed Object>
body:
### Tested versions

4.8.dev3, 4.8.dev5

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev5 - Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor (1920x1080 @ 60.04 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Graphics (ADL GT2) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1235U (12 threads) - 7.48 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

I found an issue when using a typed `for` loop with an array literal containing a previously freed object:

`for class_instance: Class in [class_instance_1, class_instance_2]:`

Godot recognizes that the array should be treated as an `Array[Class]`, but typed-array validation appears to reject a `<Freed Object>` value without considering the declared type of the variable. This appears inconsistent with `null`. I would expect the freed-object reference to be accepted by the typed array in the same way as `null`, since the variable itself is statically known to have type `Class`.

This does not appear to cause a functional problem beyond these erroneous error messages:

```
Attempted to set an invalid (previously freed?) object instance into a 'TypedArray'.
  <C++ Error>   Method/function failed. Returning: false
  <C++ Source>  ./core/variant/container_type_validate.h:97 @ _internal_validate_object()
```

```
Condition "!_p->typed.validate(value, "set")" is true.
  <C++ Source>  core/variant/array.cpp:518 @ set()
```

### Steps to reproduce

```gdscript
var ur1 := UndoRedo.new()
var ur2 := UndoRedo.new()

func _init() -> void:
	# This is fine: ur1 = null
	ur1.free()
	for ur: UndoRedo in [ur1, ur2]:
		print(ur)
```

Paste the above code inside any script.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A just paste the code snippet in any script.
